newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa prime rate seen cut by September - survey.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa prime rate seen cut by September - survey.

text.p: South Africa's prime interest rate would fall by 50 basis points to 19.75 percent by September, WorldGroup Banking said in its latest interest rate forecast.
Six economists participating in the July survey forecast prime -- which is currently at 20.25 percent -- would shed another 50 basis points by year-end.
By June 1998 it was expected to have slipped further to 18.25 percent.
Economists also forecast other rates to continue heading south over the next quarter.
The 90-day BA rate was seen falling 100 basis points over the next quarter, and losing a further 100 basis points to December 1997 and June 1998 respectively.
The most likely value for the 12-month NCD rate was estimated at 15.20 percent by September, 14.60 percent by December and 14.05 percent by June next year.
The BA rate is currently at between 15.10 to 15.25 percent, while 12-month NCD rates were last quoted between 15.50 to 15.70 percent.

On the debt market, the yield on the E168 stock was forecast to fall to 14.18 percent -- from its most recent level of 14.55 percent -- but could slip as low as 13.63 percent within the quarter. By year-end the stock would most likely yield 13.78 percent.

Economists said the barely significant outflows of foreign exchange after the easing of forex controls at the beginning of the month should have given government confidence in further relaxations or in dropping interest rates.
Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said last week that only 25 million rand had left the country in the first two weeks of July.
"However, the high level of short-term foreign debt should provide pause for thought in considering the effect that interest rate easing will have on the exchange rate," they said.
Other factors that needed to be monitored were labour uncertainties and the gold price, given that gold exports still made up a disproportionate part of South Africa's foreign earnings.
